assessment.nobel_worthiness: KPZ is a textbook example of the kind of result I value: a minimal stochastic growth equation that defines a universality class with non-Gaussian, exactly characterized fluctuations, now appearing across interfaces, polymer physics, random matrices and quantum fluids. The Takeuchi liquid-crystal turbulence experiments supply the missing close contact with experiment, quantitatively reproducing Tracy-Widom-type statistics.
assessment.attribution: Kardar and Zhang are clear originators of the 1986 equation with Parisi, whose related work was already recognized in 2021 and who is not among the credited names. Takeuchi gives the decisive experimental confirmation of the universal distributions. The exact solutions by mathematical physicists (e.g. Spohn, Sasamoto, Prahofer, Corwin, Quastel) are not in the supplied credit, so the fairness of this triple is the main question.
assessment.maturity: Theory is nearly four decades old, and the experimental confirmation and later cold-atom and other realizations are independent and reproducible. The interpretation is stable and mature; recognition is timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Omitted mathematical-physics contributors to exact solutions may be seen as having decisive credit.
Some of my recollection of the experimental lineage is from memory and not independently verified.
Overlap with the 2021 prize for complex systems could be read as redundancy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new field in which interaction strength is tuned by twist angle, producing correlated insulators and superconductivity in a clean, tunable platform. The Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band prediction is a simple continuum model with a striking quantitative consequence, which suits a physicist who likes clean models confirmed by experiment.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 theory prediction of flat bands at a magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity. This is a natural theory-plus-experiment triple, though the independent contributions of Dean/Young groups and others on moire platforms are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent groups and spawning a large literature, though the nature of the superconductivity and correlated states is still debated. Recognition is plausible but the field is still evolving.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconducting phase is unresolved.
Other contributors to the experimental discovery of moire physics may merit consideration.
Whether the field is mature enough for a prize is arguable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators gave a new classification of band insulators with protected edge and surface states, a conceptually deep and widely used idea that connects materials, topology and transport. It follows Haldane's 2016 recognition and is among the most important developments in condensed-matter physics since then.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 topological insulator in 2005; Molenkamp's group observed the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe wells in 2007, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, whose authors are not credited. Hasan's three-dimensional observations are also decisive but only three can share. Choosing Kane, Mele and Molenkamp leaves out three-dimensional experimental work and the BHZ prediction.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed by multiple independent experiments in two and three dimensions; the concepts are stable and have generalized to many platforms. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Credit dispute between 2D and 3D discovery contributions and omitted BHZ theory.
Four credited names exceed the three-laureate limit, forcing exclusion of Hasan.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming transition links glasses, foams, grains and emulsions through a simple, universal picture of marginal rigidity with critical scaling and isostaticity arguments. It is a strong example of a unifying mechanism across messy disordered systems, which matches my interest in universality and soft matter.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel's 1998 proposal and the subsequent O'Hern, Silbert, Liu and Nagel analysis defined the jamming point; the two credited people are the evident originators, though the contributions of collaborators such as O'Hern and Silbert and of the earlier granular-physics community are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Core ideas are reproduced in simulations and experiments, but the connection to the glass transition and the relevance of the zero-temperature critical point to real systems remain debated, so maturity is moderate.
uncertainties: Applicability to real thermal glasses is contested.
Whether the claim of universality is fully established is uncertain; my knowledge is not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory gave a controlled, non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons, exact in infinite dimensions and numerically practical, and it became the standard tool for Mott physics and correlated materials. Its logic of mapping a lattice onto a self-consistent impurity problem is a statistical-physics idea I find compelling.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimension limit, and Georges and Kotliar established the mapping onto an impurity problem; Metzner is not among the credited names, and Muller-Hartmann and Jarrell also contributed. A fair triple is possible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Widely validated and incorporated into electronic-structure methods, though quantitative accuracy for finite-dimensional systems depends on approximations. Mature.
uncertainties: Metzner's credit and the roles of Muller-Hartmann and Jarrell leave attribution unresolved.
Theory validation depends on case-by-case materials comparison.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution turned the foundations of quantum mechanics into a cryptographic principle with physical security guarantees, and the entanglement-based version links Bell nonlocality with practical protocols. Importance and originality are high, and the field is now an engineering reality.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard (BB84) and Ekert (E91) are the natural originators. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is not credited here, and this is relevant to priority.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally established over fibers and satellites, though practical security against side channels continues to be debated. Recognition follows the 2022 prize on entanglement experiments, so timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Practical security and real-world deployment gaps are still open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Geometric phases and the Aharonov-Bohm effect show that potentials and the topology of parameter space have physical consequences, underlying polarization, the quantum Hall effect, topological band theory and molecular dynamics. They are foundational ideas that are universally used and clearly understood.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov and Bohm (1959) and Berry (1984) are clear originators, but Bohm died in 1992, and Pancharatnam and Ehrenberg-Siday are precursors; a prize would require handling these priority questions.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed for decades and extremely mature. A prize is arguably overdue, though the age of the work makes the question of timeliness and living laureates relevant.
uncertainties: Bohm is deceased and not credited, and precursor attribution is complicated.
Whether the committee views the concept as unified or two separate discoveries is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cavity method and message-passing analyses extended spin-glass methods to constraint satisfaction, error-correcting codes and high-dimensional inference, giving a statistical-physics account of why and when algorithms work. This is close to my interest in understanding learning, though it builds on the spin-glass work recognized in 2021.
assessment.attribution: Mezard (with Parisi) developed the cavity method, Zecchina and collaborators the survey-propagation algorithms for random satisfiability, and Montanari the rigorous link to message passing and compressed sensing. Parisi is not among the credited names and is already a laureate, so credit allocation to the cited three is only partial.
assessment.maturity: Results are established by rigorous mathematics and applied in coding and inference, but the impact on practical algorithms is less direct than the 2024 recognition of neural networks, and the field overlaps heavily with the 2021 prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2021 prize may lower priority.
Impact on experimentally testable physics is indirect.
My recollection of individual contributions is not independently verified.
